newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE starts building huge mosque.
newsitem.headline: UAE starts building huge mosque.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has begun construction of one of the largest mosques in the world in the capital Abu Dhabi, newspapers said on Saturday.
Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Sultan bin Zaid al-Nahayan said construction of the 1.5 billion dirham ($408 million) mosque, which began on Friday, would take three and a half years, the papers said.
"It will have four 107-metre (351-foot) minarets and the main prayer hall alone can accommodate about 7,000 worshippers," the daily Khaleej Times quoted Sheikh Sultan as saying.
The mosque is being built by Italian construction joint venture Impregilo -Rizzani de Eccher.
The company has said the mosque would be the third largest in the world after those in Saudi Arabia's holy city of Mecca and Morocco.

Impregilo has said that the mosque would have a total area of 84,000 square metres (904,000 square feet) and prayer areas of 52,000 square metres (560,000 square feet), eight times the size of a football field. It would hold a total of 20,000 people.
